bibliographic.title: Systematic literature review on bias mitigation in generative AI
bibliographic.authors: Juveria Afreen; Mahsa Mohaghegh; Maryam Doborjeh
bibliographic.citation_apa: Afreen, J., Mohaghegh, M., & Doborjeh, M. (2025). Systematic literature review on bias mitigation in generative AI. AI and Ethics, 5, 4789–4841. https://doi.org/10.1007/s43681-025-00721-9

methodology.sector: multiple domains including text, image, audio, video; references to healthcare, transportation, and finance for LLM use
methodology.technology_context: Generative Artificial Intelligence across text, image, audio, and video modalities; large language models referenced in financial loan assessment and decision-making contexts

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed systematic literature review on bias mitigation in generative AI, explicitly covering GAI/LLMs, fairness, accountability, monitoring, and sensitive-sector applications. However, the provided text centers on bias types, causes, and mitigation across GAI modalities rather than conversational governance, chatbots, guardrails, observability, or human oversight in conversational systems. It is relevant as supporting evidence on fairness/accountability governance in GAI but not as central evidence for conversational governance in regulated LLM systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Confirm in full text whether included studies address conversational AI, dialogue systems, or operational governance mechanisms beyond general bias mitigation.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on front matter and early pages only. SLR protocol, search strategy, inclusion criteria, and synthesis methods are not visible in the supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: The study is clearly framed as a systematic review on GAI bias mitigation with coherent claims on causes and strategies, but supplied text lacks detail on review protocol and synthesis. Relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM environments is indirect.

coding.theme: Bias and fairness governance in generative AI
coding.subtheme: Mitigation strategies across text, image, audio, and video modalities
rq_alignment: partial alignment via bias/fairness/accountability in GAI
weak alignment to conversational governance and operational controls

synthesis.main_claim: The paper conducts a systematic literature review mapping types, causes, and mitigation strategies for bias in generative AI across multiple modalities, arguing that interdisciplinary collaboration and ongoing monitoring are essential for equitable AI.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured review framing of bias in GAI, including technical and non-technical mitigation approaches and emphasis on fairness, accountability, and trustworthy AI.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied excerpts do not report review search strategy, study selection counts, quality appraisal of included studies, or explicit limitations section.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on bias/fairness/accountability and monitoring in GAI/LLM contexts; not a primary source for conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, tracing, human handoff, or post-deployment operational governance in regulated conversational systems.
